text:
Incident Bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx and timeouts observed for /v1/embeddings in eu-west-1 over the last 3m. Automated GeoDNS failover not triggered. Pager alerted.
Maria G.: ack - I'm on call. paging net-eng. sla impact?
PagerDuty: P1 page sent to oncall. escalation under 5m.
Sanjay P.: looking. quick checks: Route53 health checks show intermittent failures for eu-west-1 origin healthcheck-embeddings-eu. Cloudflare shows some resolver errors for our customer-facing CNAMEs.
Lee T.: can you paste the healthcheck logs?
Sanjay P.: sure.
Sanjay P.: ```
2026-04-08T14:01:02Z healthcheck-embeddings-eu FAIL -- timeout connecting to 10.2.33.12:443
2026-04-08T14:02:12Z healthcheck-embeddings-eu PASS
2026-04-08T14:03:45Z healthcheck-embeddings-eu FAIL -- TLS handshake error
```
Maria G.: ok mix of networking TLS/resolver failures. initial hypothesis: upstream DNS/route flap in eu region causing requests to land on unhealthy VMs or return SERVFAIL.
Jonah K.: I'm running `dig` against the geo record from a paris resolver: `dig +short embeddings.redwood-inference.com @8.8.8.8` returns the eu-west-1 CNAME then an NXDOMAIN intermittently.
Maria G.: @Cloudflare Monitor what does your status page say?
Cloudflare Monitor: Incident posted: "Partial DNS resolver failures affecting EU public resolvers" - https://status.cloudflare.com/incidents/abcd-xyz (updated 8m ago). Some resolvers returning SERVFAIL for queries with EDNS0.
Ava (Customer Success): seeing multiple support tickets from EU customers reporting timeouts and increased latency, one higher-visibility customer (Acme Health) opened a P1.
Maria G.: impact summary: P1 for Acme Health, P2 for ~10 customers in EU. Embeddings API 5xx rate ~12% in last 5m, latency spike to 4-8s for routing retries.
Lee T.: immediate mitigation options: 1) Flip GeoDNS weight to 0 for eu-west-1 so traffic moves to us-east-1; 2) Force Route53 failover record to point to a healthy region; 3) Ask Cloudflare to disable EDNS for our zone (only if they recommend).
Sanjay P.: we should prefer controlled routing change rather than forcing Cloudflare. I'll run a quick health check sweep across origins then update Route53 failover.
Jonah K.: note: DNS caches with >60s TTL could take time. What TTL do we have?
Maria G.: current GeoDNS TTL is 120s. minimal but still means some cache lag. we can reduce to 30s but change won't propagate to caches that already have 120s.
Maria G.: I'm going to coordinate the change. @Sanjay take Route53, @Lee take Cloudflare comms/contact, @Jonah prep runbook for handoff.
Sanjay P.: doing Route53 update now: switching weighted record embeddings.geo -> weight 0 for eu-west-1, weight increased on us-east-1. applying..
Sanjay P.: ```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"embeddings.geo.redwood-inference.com","Type":"CNAME","SetIdentifier":"eu-west-1","Weight":0,"TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"eu-west-1-failover.redwood-inference.net."}]}}]}'
```
NetEng Bot: Change submitted, change id: C2A3B4. Expected propagation: ~30-60s for new authoritative records.
Maria G.: updating incident timeline and customer comms draft. Ava, can you start the customer outreach for Acme Health (provide mitigation steps and ETA)?
Ava (Customer Success): on it. I'll send the initial note and offer temporary routing to us-east.
Jonah K.: running synthetic checks from multiple EU probes to verify behavior.
Jonah K.: probe results: from paris -> now resolving to us-east-1 IPs for ~60% of queries, remaining probes still hit eu-west-1 returning SERVFAIL.
Sanjay P.: further mitigation: enabling Route53 failover to force health-checked secondary endpoint (already pre-provisioned). initiating failover.
Sanjay P.: done. Failover active.
Maria G.: good. monitoring metrics. 5xx rate dropping to 2% in last 3m. latency improving.
Cloudflare Monitor: note: Cloudflare has bulk mitigation in progress for resolver errors but recommends customers implement failover while their mitigation rolls out.
Lee T.: opening a postmortem ticket and assigning to network team for follow-up with Cloudflare and to review EDNS0 interactions.
Ava (Customer Success): Acme Health confirmed reduced errors after routing change, they reopened the ticket to monitor, thanked us for quick response.
Maria G.: summary for incident channel: cause = upstream DNS/resolver failures and intermittent TLS handshakes in eu-west-1; immediate mitigation = Route53 weighted failover + healthcheck failover to us-east-1; impact = temporary P1 for one customer, several P2s; status = degraded -> recovering.
Maria G.: I'll hand this to @Jonah for the oncall overlap and write the mitigation/playbook in the ticket. handoff at 1742001200 UTC.
Jonah K.: ack taking over. Handoff notes: steps performed, change ids C2A3B4, failover activated, customer comms drafted. monitoring for 1h then we revert if stable.
Maria G.: thanks team. leaving the channel. please add any follow-ups to NETENG-842 in the postmortem template. :white_check_mark:
Jonah K.: creating the incident postmortem now and will ping infra for a cross-check with Cloudflare next week.
Incident Bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status -> recovering; next update scheduled in 30m or when status changes.
